item.title: Week 6, Djibouti 2026 Spring Season.
item.content:encoded:
As the new week began with a fresh group, memories of the previous one, where the action had been slow, were still lingering. During the briefing, I brought it up, and with crossed fingers we headed back out to sea, hoping for a turnaround.

From the very first day, things looked completely different. The water was alive, almost like a soup of baitfish, and it instantly lifted our expectations. It didn’t take long to confirm it: the fishing was on. As we reached our spots, we watched bait being smashed by big predators; at times it felt like the ocean itself was feeding.

Nearly every cast brought action, mackerel, GT, barracuda. Mackerel, in particular, showed up in huge numbers, keeping things exciting even during slower moments with their explosive strikes and acrobatic jumps. The rhythm of the day would rise and fall, bursts of chaos followed by quieter spells, then back again.

Of course, no trip comes without its challenges. This week’s struggle came in the form of lost big fish. Despite solid hooksets, they kept coming off, leaving us exchanging those all-too-familiar blank looks. It was frustrating, losing fish across multiple spots, at all times of day, even from the shore, but it never stopped us from pushing harder, believing the next one would stick.

That persistence finally paid off. During a long afternoon session that stretched into the night, we landed a proper fish, one that marked a new personal best for our guest and lifted the whole crew.

We closed the week on a positive note. With the big fish activity dropping on the final day, the group shifted focus to species fishing and made the most of it. All in all, it was a strong week.

Now we head into the final stretch of the season, hoping to finish on a high note and head home for some well-earned rest.

item.title: Welcome To Paradise - By Pål-Severin Båtnes
item.content:encoded:
At the end of November, we went on a «little» fishing trip to Venezuela, specifically to Los Roques, a large coral archipelago located just a short flight from Caracas. From past experiences, I know it can pay off to go fishing in countries marked by political unrest and civil conflict—places the Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs advises against visiting. In such areas, fishing pressure is reduced, and the fishing improves. The fishing here was nothing short of extraordinary, and all advice not to go was nonsense.

Joining me on the trip was Bjarte Kristoffersen, who has been my fishing buddy since our teenage years. However, this was his first experience with tropical fly fishing, and it turned out to be his greatest fishing adventure ever.

Los Roques is a paradise. The archipelago has about 2,000 inhabitants, and the inflight to Gran Roque feels like a dream. It’s a car-free village where instead of asphalt is white sand. The area consists of more than 300 small islands and cays, renowned for their beautiful beaches, crystal-clear waters, and abundant marine life.

After a short walk on the beach on our first evening, we realized what lay ahead. The waters were teeming with rolling tarpons weighing up to 50 kg, and billions of sardines and minnows were being hunted by various predatory fish. Every day, we went out with a boat and guide, who took us to one dream spot after another. Our main target was the big tarpons. The thrill of casting a fly to a fish as long as ourselves, often just a rod’s length away, is hard to describe.

But it wasn’t just the tarpons that gave us lifelong memories. Bjarte also caught his first parrotfish on his third cast with the fly. And then there was the nearly impossible permit fish. Over three days in “permit heaven,” we managed to hook a total of 9 large permits, but unfortunately, we only landed one. It was over 80 cm long. The last one I lost was tailing in 110 cm of water, and it must have been at least 120–130 cm. We followed it with the boat as it shot off like a rocket without stopping, but eventually, the loop on the flyline snapped.

For 12 days, we had an exhilarating fishing experience. Fly hooks were bent and broken, leaders snapped as if they were made of silk, and our forearm muscles were as exhausted as after the Vasaloppet ski race.

Los Roques has not seen the last of us. After six trips with Wild Sea Expedition, I must say they are incredible at facilitating truly exceptional fishing adventures.

item.title: Socotra Fishing - Monster GT
item.content:encoded:
Back to expeditions

Socotra fishing: Monster GT

Socotra, the best GT destination in the world is now possible to fish again.

A regular flight is operating from Abu Dhabi to Socotra.

ABOUT SOCOTRA

This island, about 120 km long, is considered the windiest in the world and is beaten by very strong currents, factors that make the sea impassable for about 7 months a year in the most productive spots. The island is also known for its many endemic dragon blood trees and numerous other species of plants, birds, reptiles, and insects that live only here, so much to be called “The Galapagos of the Indian Ocean”, and is recognized as a natural heritage of ' Humanity by UNESCO.

The island is not very populated by people, there aren’t any accommodations with the exception of a few spartan camps, and fishing villages are few and far from everything, sometimes reachable only by boat.

Thanks to these characteristics, often in beautiful places for fishing, with high cliffs overlooking the sea, sand dunes, or uninhabited islands, which transmit sensations enough to make us think about fishing in prehistoric times.

Wild Sea Expedition has dedicated over 10 years to the exploration of this place, but also to fishing in the Indian Ocean in general. We know every rock, current, and season which will take you to the incredible thing about this island… places that we explored and found will give you the average size of gt that attacks the popper and it has no comparison to the whole world! So in 90% of the cases, we have a fish over 40 kg behind our lure, and in the remaining 10% with fish over 30 kg, enough to embarrass even the most experienced.

This feature is certainly due to several factors: primarily the abundance of forage fish such as rainbow runners and fusiliers, combined with the lack of fishing pressure in these waters and strong currents that transport large quantities of nutrients.

In addition to the obvious fortunate position, in the middle of the ocean current that comes from the South favors the upwelling, which brings nutrients to the surface layers. For several months the winds are very violent, causing sea conditions often prohibitive, and thus preventing continuous fishing by local fishermen, who still do not have huge resources. In practice, you can fish well and be safe only for a little less than four months a year, from October to November and from March to April.

FISH & SEASON

Socotra is in the north Indian Ocean, so almost all the fish of this sea are present.

The most important sportfish is GT, but in October there is a huge migration of Spanish Mackerel, and a migration of pelagic crabs, that float on the water causing a continuous feeding by many kinds of trevally such as Golden Trevally, Yellow Spotted Trevally, Bludger Trevally, and Black Tip Trevally.

Many kinds of coral fish are present such as Red Snapper, Green Jobfish, Rusty Jobfish, Coral Trout, and different species of grouper and emperor.

From shore, it is possible to find Indian Permit, Bonefish, small Threadfin, Leerfish, Bream, and Bluefin Trevally.

On jigging it is possible to catch everything, amberjack is present too.

Sharks are also present but rarely hooked on lures, the most catched are Fox Shark on Jigging.

The best seasons to fish in Socotra are Autumn and Spring because in Summer and Winter the wind is very strong and the sea very rough.

BASE CAMP ACCOMMODATION

In Socotra, the only way to arrange a trip will be by touring a camp run by us.

The camp consists of 2 large tents for six people, one as a dining room and one as a camp kitchen, and for sleep, every fisherman has a big double tend equipped with mattresses, sheets and pillows, 1 tank of 2000 liters of fresh water, shower box, rods holder, a cook with a camp kitchen, an interpreter and a jeep always available. Satellite phones are also available.

About food, in Socotra the variety is very limited, usually, it is possible to eat pasta, rice, bread cooked day by day, beans, eggs, vegetable sauce, fish, biscuits, soft cheese, lamb, chicken, honey and sometimes Nutella. During the fishing season, it is possible to get some lobster. Usually, meat is consumed once or twice a week, because of the limited availability.

Soft drinks are included in the price, alcoholic drinks are allowed but not sales, and clients can bring their own drinks from other airports.

Concerning the boats, the only solution at present is the use of local fishing boats, fiberglass boats about 8 meters long and equipped with 40 hp engines. Every boat and group has its international guide.

The standard trips are based on 4 clients, fishing from 2 boats.

High-quality silent generator for electricity in our camp.

TRIP SCHEDULE OPTIONS

STANDARD TRIP

The standard trip includes 6 full days of fishing, and it’s the best way to have the first approach with Socotra. In this journey, you will have your first contact with the reality of this world, and of course with the brutality of this fishing.

EXTREME ITINERARY

This will be probably the wildest, extreme and most amazing trip you will enjoy in your life, visiting some of the most remote frontiers for huge Gts. For this trip we don’t have a definitive schedule, because it has to be built time by time in accordance with the client request. It can be from 6 to 13 days, and also logistics, organization and costs can be different time by time.

HOW TO GET THERE

The clients have to provide their own international flight to Cairo or Dubai, Wild Sea Expedition will provide the flight from Cairo to Socotra or Dubai to Socotra.

SAFETY & HEALTH

Currently coming to Socotra is completely safe for tourists, and the direct flights from other countries make the travel easy and smooth.

About Socotra, the island is completely safe and pirate-free.

Regarding health, there aren’t tropical diseases like yellow fever or typhus in Socotra, and malaria has been extinct. 

On top of that, there are two new hospitals managed by Saudi Arabia and the Emirates, where is possible to have high-quality health assistance in case of emergency.

Clients must be covered by travel/medical insurance and medical evacuation.


VACCINATIONS

No vaccinations are required for this trip.

Visa

We do your visa with a copy of your passport by email. A passport must be valid for at least 6 months and with no visas for Israel.

WHAT IS INCLUDED

  • All the services in Socotra

NOT INCLUDED

  • Visa (provided by WSE)

  • Flights Cairo to Socotra or Dubai to Socotra (provided by WSE)

  • Tips

  • Extra for a single room in Socotra.

TECHNIQUE & EQUIPMENT

Popping

What we do in Socotra, is not popping, is extreme popping, and is the top of the top in terms of technique, experience, and brutality. Here every part of your equipment can be broken, from the hooks to the reels.

Due to the conformation of the fishing spot, sometimes the conditions became really extreme, first, the medium size of the fish is incredible, the water is shallow, and all around are present many rocks and wrecks, and everything is done during strong current conditions.

Now imagine hooking an over 60, and imagine what can happen to the tackle.

Because of this, everything in the equipment has to be extra strong: the rod has to be a PE 10, the shock leader up to 250 lb matched with a short bite tippet made of kevlar cord, to prevent the cut by the fish that suck down the lure. Fluorocarbon is not enough, sometimes it also happens to find a dead GT with a popper deep in the throat just after losing a fish for the leader cutting off the leader.

About the terminal, split rings have to be only the biggest from BKK. BKK Crusader single hook in size 8/0, 9/0, BKK Raptor size 3/0, 4/0, 5/0…BKK Split Ring - 51 sizes 8 and 9.

Tuff line 130 lb, power pro 170 lb, also if the strength seems, all these lines are the same.

About lures you must have some big and noisy poppers, our favorites are Craft Bait gt3, Fcl Labo ebi pop and extreme, Orion cono cone, and Patriot Design master bomb.

More than poppers, sinking sticks are always a good weapon, our favorites are Orion bigfoot and plug tropic, and we sell special handmade sticks specially designed and made for us.

At the end some big floating sticks can be a good choice when fish are lazy.

Light casting

Light casting can be done from the boat and from shore. From the boat, we suggest carrying a PE3 rod with some minnow and sinking lures to fish around rocks targeting Emperor, Groper, and Snapper, and some small stickbait and popper for bluewater fishing targeting Dorado, Spanish Mackerel, and different kinds of Trevally. From the shore, you can fish PE3 for bigger species, or go with a PE1-1,5 rod casting metal jig and small minnow for Bluefin Trevally, various species of Trevally, Threadfin, Bonefish, and Pompano.

Jigging

On Jigging it is possible to catch everything, every species of Trevally, Groupers, Amberjack, Jobfish, and Yellowfin Tuna. The best way is to bring two Jigging rods, a PE2-3 for shallower water targeting Trevally and rocky species in 30 to 60 mt of water with 80-150 gr jigs, and a heavy setup for PE4-5 for deeper fishing targeting Amberjack, Grouper, and Jobfish, with jigs from 150 to 300 gr.

For all the fanatics of GT, fishing in Socotra is
an experience without parallel!

item.title: Pesca in Sudan: Nubian Flat
item.content:encoded:
Torna alle spedizioni

Pesca in Sudan: Nubian Flat

Temporarily Unavailable

La pesca

Il viaggio comincia da Port Sudan, a bordo delle nostre barche da crociera MY Don Questo o MSY Elegante

Il Sudan rappresenta ad oggi uno dei luoghi più intoccato dalla pesca professionale, e con una scarsissima pressione locale, dato che i quasi 650 km di costa sono quasi interamente disabitati, e la popolazione locale ha una cultura prettamente pastorale e trae scarsissime risorse dal mare.

Grazie all’esperienza maturata nel corso degli anni e alla profonda conoscenza del mare Sudanese, Wild Sea Expedition garantisce il miglior servizio e i migliori itinerari di pesca  in accordo con le condizioni.

Al momento il Sudan è l'ultima novità nel mondo delle destinazione di pesca a mosca, e questo rende il viaggio ancora più eccitante dato il quantitativo di flats e zone ancora da esplorare., Durante la prima stagione esplorativa abbiamo scoperto stupendi flats vergini, realmente infestati di Triggerfish, pesce ancora poco conosciuto ma veramente eccitante da pescare, spesso in acqua molto bassa

Inoltre sono presenti in buona quantità GT, Red Snapper e Bluefin Trevally, ma anche Permit, Milkfish, Bumphead Parrotfish ed enormi Bonefish, e altre specie da barriera corallina sono presenti e possibili da catturare. Altre specie da barriera come Cernie, Coral Trout e Napoleon Wrasse sono presenti e possibili a mosca, insieme ai Dogtooth tuna insidiabili a dredging per chi non teme la fatica.

NB: solo permessi solo ami senza ardiglione per la sicurezza dei pescatori e per il rispetto dei pesci.

ALLOGGIO

Dal semplice ma confortevole caicco a una vera e propria nave in acciaio, siamo in grado di offrire una varia e unica offerta di viaggi in modalità ‘’liveaboard’’ per le nostre spedizioni in Mar Rosso. Cabine singole o doppie, doccia calda, aria condizionata, cabine spaziose, grandi spazi living e pasti eccellenti preparati dal nostro team; tutto questo rende le nostre spedizioni al pari di destinazioni più blasonate intorno al mondo, ma senza perdere la nostra essenza selvaggia ed originale.

MSY Elegante

L’Elegante è un bellissimo Caicco in legno a due alberi, in grado di offrire un comfort elevato grazie all’ottima distribuzione degli spazi interni ed esterni. Affascinante e romantica, è la barca perfetta per godersi la fine delle giornate ammirando i tramonti Sudanesi, ancorati in calme ed isolate lagune. La barca ha sei cabine doppie per gli ospiti, con bagno privato e doccia, aria condiziona. Gestione Italiana con 25 anni di esperienza in Mar Rosso.

velocità     10 nodi

lunghezza    25 metri

larghezza     6,5 metri

cabine        3 matrimoniali, 4 doppie con bagno e doccia

MY Don Questo

Costruito per lavorare nei mari del Nord, eccellente capacità di navigazione e di sostenere le condizioni meteo marine più avverse. L’imbarcazione è in grado di ormeggiare e stazionare in luoghi e condizioni in cui la maggior parte delle altre barche da crociera dovrebbero cercare ancoraggi riparati. Questo permette di ottimizzare i tempi morti e di navigazioni durante le crociere di pesca, e di offrire svariate opzioni in caso di deteriorazioni delle condizioni marine.

Ciò è particolarmente importante nell’itinerario Deep South.

Estremamente confortevole per 6 ospiti. Gestione Italiana con 25 anni di esperienza in Sudan.

velocità     9 nodi

lunghezza   33 metri

larghezza     8 metri

cabine 7 cabine doppie, 1 tripla tutte con lavandino. 4 docce e 5 bagni per gli ospiti

PROGRAMMI DI VIAGGIO

Viaggio Standard

Il viaggio Standard comprende 6 giorni completi di pesca, pescando ogni giorno in una zona diversa. Per ridurre la pressione di pesca cambiamo area di settimana in settimana. Questo è il nostro viaggio più popolare, con una durata classica di 6 giorni avrete la possibilità di vedere il meglio che i Nubian Flats hanno da offrire.

Viaggio Extended

Il viaggio Extended può avere una durata variabile dai 9 ai 13 giorni di pesca, il che rende possibile pescare numerosi spot con caratteristiche diverse, e avere più tempo da dedicare a target specifici come GT o Bonefish. In questo viaggio sarà possibile raggiungere le migliori aree per GT, Triggerfish e Bonefish.

Viaggio Deep South

Il viaggio Deep South può avere una durata variabile dai 9 ai 13 giorni a bordo del MY Don Questo. In questo itinerario sarà possibile esplorare aree estremamente remote e completamente intoccate. Questo viaggio vi porterà nelle acque più vergini del Sudan a bordo di un vero e proprio battello da ricerca, il più lontano dalla costa e più vicino al confine con l’Eritrea. In questa spedizione è possibile visitare i migliori spot al mondo per i Triggerfish e con una incredibile abbondanza di specie da barriera corallina.

IN ACCORDO CON LE ESIGENZE DEI NOSTRI CLIENTI OFFRIAMO UNA GUIDA INTERNAZIONALE OGNI DUE PESCATORI

Come arrivare

In questo momento l'opzione migliore per raggiungere Port Sudan è volare via Dubai con Emirates o altre compagnie. Da Dubai a Port Sudan esistere solo un volo bisettimanale il Lunedi e il Venerdì con Fly Dubai.

Sicurezza e salute

La parte costiera e in generale il nord del Sudan, sono aree sicure per il turismo, non c'è guerra o altri problemi di sicurezza, la gente del posto è molto tranquilla e amichevole, e molti turisti visitano il paese ogni anno. Anche il mare è completamente sicuro, la pirateria non esiste, non sono mai stati registrati attacchi negli ultimi 40 anni ed il mare è ben sorvegliato dalla marina militare Sudanese.

Circa la sicurezza degli ospiti, le guide di pesca sono formate nel primo soccorso, in ogni caso tutti i clienti sono obbligati a viaggiare coperti da un’assicurazione medica di viaggio. Tutti gli ospiti sono tenuti a firmare una liberatoria di scarico di responsabilità nei confronti di Wild Sea Travel.

Vaccinazioni

Nessuna vaccinazione è richiesta per questo viaggio

Visti

Wild Sea Expedition provvede al vostro visto turistico semplicemente con la copia del vostro passaporto via email. 

Il passaporto deve avere 6 mesi di validità e non avere visti per Israele.

Che cosa è incluso

  • Sistemazione In cabine doppie su MY Don Questo o MSY Elegante , pensione completa.

  • Crociera con partenza e rientro a Port Sudan.

  • Tutti i trasferimenti a terra.

  • Acqua Minerale acqua, tè / / caffè / succo di frutta inclusi.


Il prezzo non include

  • Visto

  • Soft drink e bevande alcoliche.

  • Mance e spese di natura personale

  • Volo internazionale


PESCI E ATTREZZATURE

I flat Sudanesi sono densamente popolati di Triggerfish, di Gt spesso di ottima taglia, enormi Barracuda, Squali Pinna Nera, Bonefish e Permit.

Pescando dal bordo della barriera le catture più comuni sono Gt, Snapper, Bluefin ed altri pesci di barriera come Cernie, Coral Trout e Mangrove Jack.

Anche Milkfish di taglie mostruose sono ben presenti, con esemplari ben oltre i 20 kg, a patto di avere la fortuna di trovare le condizioni di mare ideali in cui questi pesci si nutrono in superficie.

Anche Bumphead Parrotfish sono presenti con taglie difficilmente riscontrabili altrove, pesci sopra i 40 kg sono già stati allamati, ma purtroppo persi fra ami rotti, finali tagliati nel reef e slamate.

Di seguito i set up raccomandati per affrontare questo viaggio:


Bonefish e Triggerfish

Una canna da 9 piedi per coda 9 abbinata ad un mulinello da mare con ottima frizione, caricato con 200 metri di backing da 50 libbre ed una coda galleggiante di alta qualità, molto decentrata per lanciare nel vento, per acque tropicali.

Bumphead Parrotfish, Triggerfish e  Milkfish

Una canna da 9 piedi per coda 10 con un mulinello di alta qualità caricato con 200 metri di backing da 60 libbre ed una coda galleggiante.

GT, Bluefin Trevally e varie specie di barriera

Una canna 9 piedi per coda 12  con un mulinello dotato di frizione di altissima qualità caricato con 200 o più metri di backing da 80 libbre.

Fondamentale è avere una coda con un core ad alta resistenza per poter strappare i pesci dal corallo, la nostra scelta favorita è la Rio Gt special che ha un core da 65 libbre.

Finali, code e attrezzatura di riserva

  • 3 leader da 9 piedi da 22lb specifici da mare.

  • 1 bobina da 17lb di fluorocarbon da tippet

  • 1 bobina da 130lb o 150lb di Sufix Zippy Nylon

  • 1 coda 9 galleggiante di riserva

  • 2 code 12 galleggianti di riserva

  • 1 canna per coda 9 o 10 di riserva

  • 1 canna per coda 12 di riserva

Mosche

E 'fondamentale che i pescatori portino la giusta selezione di mosche, montate nel modo giusto e con i materiali corretti. Avere la giusta selezione di mosche fa una enorme differenza in termini di strikes.

Ecco la nostra selezione di mosche per i Nubian Flats:

  • Spawning Shrimp #6 x 4

  • JC Sand Prawn #4 x 2

  • Rolling Bead Crab #4 x 4

  • Tan Merkin Tan #2 x 2

  • Tailler’s Delight Olive #4 x 2

  • Tailer’s Delight Tan #4 x 2

  • Velcro Crab Tan #2 x4

  • Avalon Permit Shrimp #2 x 4

  • Gt Brush Fly Black, Black and Purple #6/0 x 2

  • Sempre Black and Purple #6/0 x 2

  • Poodle #6/0 x 2

  • Popper NYAP #6/0 x 2

  • Clouser Chartreuse and White #2 x 4

Al momento il Sudan è l'ultima novità al mondo di destinazione per la pesca a mosca.

item.title: Peru - The Mighty Arapaima
item.content:encoded:
Back to expeditions

Peru Fishing: The Mighty Arapaima

The reason why you should get yourself into the Jungle and try to tame an Arapaima, is the Arapaima itself.

ABOUT ARAPAIMA

The reason why you should get yourself into the Jungle and try to tame an Arapaima is the Arapaima itself. We think that every trip, every destination has something special to offer, after we fished ourselves in the Peruvian Jungle we got really hooked on this fish. We fished for many different species around the world, but Arapaima is a truly unique animal, it’s a crossing between a snake and a fish when it jumps is just breathtaking and spectacular, it has lungs and after the fighting, you have to make it breathe out of the water, it’s a living fossil of 23 millions of years, the head is amazingly carved and the scales and fins are just incredible, making this fish looking like artwork, is just amazing to hold one.

And everything is framed by a wild and remote jungle environment.

ARAPAIMA GIGAS LODGE

The lodge is located in the heart of the Amazon jungle surrounded by wilderness with incredible wildlife. You might see the harpy eagle, pink dolphins, giant otters, caimans, and many different bird species. The area has never been a location for sport fishing before. We have the honor to operate in these pristine lakes and rivers.

We did a fly fishing trip in the jungle for research purposes for five weeks in 2017/2018, fishing some very remote lakes that even the local natives had never seen.

The result was very good, on our first exploratory trip for fly fishing we landed a fish well over 120 kg. At the Arapaima Gigas Lodge, we practice all the fishing techniques according to anglers’ wishes, fly fishing, spinning, and baiting.

SEASON

During the rainy season, the river floods and rises six or seven meters allowing the Arapaima to swim into the jungle ponds. The water drops in the dry season so the Arapaima are trapped in the jungle lakes. Fishing seasons occur during the dry seasons of December, January, and February.

During the dry season, it is also possible to find rain and rising water, this requires the fisherman’s persistence and adaptability.

TRIP SCHEDULE

The trip includes 10 full days of fishing, so it will be possible to discover very remote areas almost completely unfished. On this trip, you will visit the most virgin waters of the amazon.

DAY 1:

  • Arrive and stay at the hotel, in the early morning (3:00 AM)

  • transfer to the river by bus (approx 6h), boat transfer (10h),

  • overnight in a hotel.

DAY 2:

  • Early morning departure by boat, approx 6 hr.

  • Arrival at the lodge, half-day fishing.

DAY 3-11:

  • Nine full days of fishing.

DAY 13:

  • Half fishing day lunch and transfer back.

DAY 14:

  • Boat and bus transfer back to Quito.

THE FISHING

In this area, we fish in oxbow lakes. The lakes are in general closed off inside the jungle and are not very affected by the level of the river. There are no beaches to fish from, so all spin / fly fishing for arapaima is made from small fiberglass boats. The Arapaimas in these lakes are very big compared to other places in the world, and it is possible to catch fish measuring over 2 meters. A bit of hard work is needed to reach some lakes and good physical condition is required for this trip.

The fishing for Arapaima is very similar to Pike fishing, big lures, jerkbait, rubber shad, big bucktail flies, worked slowly close to the grass patch, not making noise on the boat, being silent, rowing gently and keep casting till an amazing strong pull.

SPECIES

Arapaima, Peacock bass.

ACCOMMODATION

Our camp is built on two local traditional wooden huts, accommodating 6 anglers each. Every guest will be sleeping in a tent with a mosquito net. We have a trained chef with many years of experience. There is a generator to enable guests to charge electronics.

We also have a refrigerator, a big gas kitchen, a shower and toilet, and dispensers for hot/ cold water.

WHAT IS INCLUDED

• Accommodation in the Lodge

• Transfer and returning from the Lodge

• Mineral water, tea, coffee, juice and all meals in the Lodge


NOT INCLUDED

• Visa

• Tips

• International flights

• Transfer to and from the airport to hotel

• Hotel stays


HOW  TO  GET THERE

In order to fly to Quito (Ecuador) we suggested searching for your best flight options. There are several flights every day from all around the world. From Quito, our crew will take you to our lodge.

SAFETY &  HEALTH

Trip insurance is required. You will be in very remote areas for the duration of your trip. Guests are required to be in good health and medical condition during their trip. Arapaima Gigas Lodge operation must be made aware of every guest’s personal, special, medical, or dietary requirements. Guests are also required to purchase general trip insurance. Also, we recommend Global Rescue insurance during your trip with us.

VACCINATION

Yellow Fever vaccination is suggested.

TACKLE AND EQUIPMENT

BAIT FISHING 

A catfish rod 150-250g 9-12 feet with a big Penn reel 6500-7500 model loaded with 150-250m braid of 80-100 LB. The thickness of the line is necessary so it is more abrasion resistant for the vegetation and for the crazy headshakes the Arapaima do when they are airborne. We use circle hooks 9/0-10/0 and for leader 130 lbs fluorocarbon or thick kevlar 1mm-1,5mm. Anglers can be more successful when targeting Arapaima with cut bait, or even better: live bait. Small whole fish on a wide gap circle hook works well. The take is very visible. Anglers should allow the line to go tight and then point the rod tip at the fish, so the circle hook can do its work. A “J” or treble hook is usually more difficult because the angler must drive the hookset into the arapaima’s bony, hard mouth. 

Terminal tackle 

  • Kevlar leader 1mm-1,5mm/Steel leader 

  • 2 x Catfish rods 150-250g 

  • 2 x Large Penn reels 6500-7500 model 

  • Circle hooks 9/0 10/0 

  • Braid 0.45mm-0,55mm Pe10 Pe12 


F LY F I S H I N G 

Arapaima 

9 feet rod 12 weight with a very high-quality saltwater reel with a strong drag, loaded with 100 or more meters of 80 lb braid. A very high- quality and high strength fly line is necessary to pull the fish out of vegetation when needed. We strongly suggest Rio GT special or Airflo GT lines. 

Peacock Bass

9 feet rod 9 weight with a high-quality saltwater disc drag reel. Load the reel with 100 or more meters of 60 lb braid. A high-quality weight-forward floating line for tropical warm water is the best choice.

Terminal and backup tackle

  • 60 lb saltwater leaders 

  • 1 x 130 or 150 lb fluorocarbon 

  • 2 x 9 weight floating line 

  • 3 x 12 weight floating line

  • 1 backup 9 or 10 weight rod 

  • 1 backup 12 weight rod 

Flies 

It’s critical that anglers carry the right selection of flies, tied in the correct way with the correct material. This will make a substantial difference in the strike rate. Our selection of flies for arapaima are baitfish flies that move lot of water 12-15cm cross-tied by /Ep fibers /Sf/Sculping fibers Wiggletail also works well, we recommend that you a high-end quality hook like tiemco 600sp 6/0 or 8/0 and Daichi saltwater black ace hooks. Color combinations for Arapaima and Peacock Bass: White/Chartreuse, Black/Red, Yellow/White, Yellow/chartreuse 

SPIN FISHING 

Arapaima

  • 120-180 grams rod Pe6- Pe8 baitcasting rod

  • Lures Tail-baits/Jerk-baits 50-90 gram 

  • Reel Penn 5500-6500model 

  • Braid 0.45-0.55mm Pe10/ Pe12 

  • Leader Kevlar 1-1.5mm/130 lb Nylon 

  • Single J hooks

Peacock Bass 

  • Leader 50lb Fluocarbon

  • 1 x Light tackle rod 30-60 gr 

  • 1 x Penn reel 3500-5500 model 

  • Braid 0.25mm-0.35 mm Pe6

  • Spinnerbaits 15-25 gr

  • Poppers 20-35 gr 

  • Crankbaits 20-40 gr 

  • Buzz baits 20-30 gr

In this trip you will visit the most virgin waters of the amazon.

item.title: Nubian Reef
item.content:encoded:
Back to expeditions

Sudan Fishing: Nubian Reef

FISH & SEASON

The journey starts from Port Sudan, on board one of our Motherboat MY Don Questo.

Sudanese area is one of the current pure unfished and pristine destinations; it comes with a 650 km coastline bordering the Red Sea and it is almost uninhabited.

As the coast offers a wide range of sceneries and seascapes (such as deepwater reefs, shallow water reefs, flat, lagoons, mangroves, and Coral) it is possible to be involved in many sport fishing as well as to spot a broad variety of fish (GTs, Coral Trout, Grouper, Emperor, Barracuda, Red Snapper, Napoleon Wrasse, Black Tip Shark, Grey Shark, Silky Shark, a remarkable population of Dogtooth Tuna, Bluefin Trevally, Titan Triggerfish, Giant Humphead Parrotfish, blue trevally, and Bonefish).

Wild Sea Expedition guarantees the best equipment to fish and visits a wide range of enchanting areas.

Since we have extensively operated over the past years and we have deepened our knowledge of the Sudanese area, Wild Sea Expedition guarantees the best service in a safe environment.


Only barbless hooks are allowed, for the safety on board and in respect of the fish

ACCOMODATION

From simple but comfortable vessels to more robust and larger boats, we have a unique diversity of LIVEABOARDS available for our expeditions in the Red Sea.
Single and double cabins, hot showers, air conditioning, spacious rooms, large solariums, and excellent meals prepared by the local team — all of this make our expeditions equivalent to acclaimed places around the globe but with our unique WILD and original essences.

For the fishing action, we use two simple and comfortable fiberglass boats of 8 meters.

DON QUESTO 

Built to work in the European North Sea. Excellent seaworthiness and ability to withstand the harshest and most extreme weather and sea conditions. The ship is able to moor/keep the station in many places and conditions in which the typical recreational diving vessel would have to run for shelter. This allows for the minimum interruption to the fishing program and offers plenty of options in the event of a sudden deterioration in the weather. This is particularly important in the South / Deep South. Extremely comfortable for six guests. Italian ownership with 25 years of experience in Sudan

​Speed:                              9 knots cruise

Length:                              33 meters

Width:                                8 meters

Cabins:                      Seven double cabins and one triple, all with a wash-hand basin with warm and cold water. Four showers and five toilets are provided for the guests.

TRIP SCHEDULE

Standard trip

The standard trip includes 6 full days of fishing, fishing every day in a different area. To reduce the fishing pressure we change zones week by week.

This is the most popular trip, and in only six days of fishing, you will be able to fish undisturbed areas.

Extended & discovery trip

The extended trips have a variable duration from 9 to 13 full days of fishing, so it will be possible to discover very remote areas almost completely unfinished. On this trip, you will visit the most virgin water of Sudan, the further North or South in accordance with season and fishing conditions. During this journey, it will be possible to visit the best areas for jigging and the best areas for popping.

HOW TO GET THERE

At the moment it is possible to get there via many places around the world. What we recommend is an Ethiopian flight over Addis Ababa because now they have flights to Port Sudan every day, and they are( for now )the cheapest flights to Sudan. In according with the trip schedule we assist you in order to get the best flight solution. 

SAFETY & HEALTH

The coastal side and generally the north of Sudan, are safe areas for tourism, there is no war or other safety problems, the local people are very quiet, and many tourists visit the mainland every year. Also, the sea is completely safe, the pirates don't exist in this area.

Regarding the guests’ safety, the fishing guides are trained in emergency first response.

All clients are asked to arrive covered by travel/medical insurance for the trip. Furthermore, all guests will sign a disclosure wavering Wild Sea Travel of any liability due to any accident.

Vaccination

No vaccinations are required for this trip

Visa

We do a tourism visa with your passport copy by email. We do your visa with a copy of your passport by email. A passport must be valid for at least 6 months and with no visas for Israel. At this moment it takes one month for your Sudan VISA to be done, so we highly recommend that as soon as you book the trip send us your passport so we can prepare your VISA on time.

WHAT IS INCLUDED

  • Accommodation in double cabins on MY Don Questo or MSY Elegante, full board.

  • Cruise leaving and returning to Port Sudan.

  • All land transportation.

  • Mineral water, tea/coffee/juice included.

NOT INCLUDED

  • Visa

  • Soft drink and alcoholic drink

  • Tips and expense of personal nature

  • International flights


TECHNIQUE AND EQUIPMENT

Popping

As the seaward side of the Sudanese coast is thick with coral reefs, seawater offers a wide variety of fish. Wild Sea Expedition is fully learned in both popping and lure casting. 

On poppers, it is possible to hook GTs, Red Snapper, Coral Trout, different kinds of Grouper and Emperor, big Barracuda, Napoleon Wrasse, Dogtooth Tuna, and Shark.

ROD: you will need a 170-200 gr rod able to hold 8-10 kg of drag, and a 100-120 gr rod to fish with 6 kg of drag

REELS: for heavy popping Stella 10000 FA, 18000 SW or Saltiga 6000, for light popping Stella 8000 FA, Stella 10000 SW and Saltiga 4500

LINE AND LEADER: for heavy popping 150 lb braid and 200 lb shock leader, for light popping a 65 lb line with a 120 lb leader work well. To connect the braid and leader we suggest a PR or FG knot.

LURES: noisy popper from 80 to 140 gr, floating stickbait about 18-24 cm, and sinking stickbait from 80 

to 150 gr.

TERMINAL TACKLE: BKK Crusader single hook in size 8/0, 9/0,10/0, 11/0 BKK GT

Rex size 5/0 and BKK Raptor size 4/0 and 5/0, BKK Split Ring - 51 size 8 and 9

Jigging

Jigging is likely the most productive technique in Sudan; many big fishes are hooked weekly.

It is well impressive the stunning concentration of Dogtooth Tuna over the Sudanese Red Sea, indeed it is quite common to hook 4 Doggies at the same time during the first drop.

Probably Sudan represents today one of the last good fisheries for big doggies, thanks to the structure of the drop-off and the low professional fishing.

The medium size is between 7 and 15 kg, even if a number of bigger ones have been recently spotted.

Other species are caught on jigging too, however, tuna represents the big majority of the catch.

ROD: the best is to get two rods, one in the 300 gr range, Instead good equipment to fight with a submarine is a powerful rod for 400-500 gr,

REELS: on the medium rod is possible to use a medium reel like Shimano Stella SW 10000 or other reels of the same size, or conventional reels with a high retrieve ratio. On the powerful rod, you will need a Stella 20000 SW or 18000 SW for speed jigging.

LINE: for medium jigging a 50-60 lb line, for heavy tackle the best option is a PE 6-8 (80-100 lb)

JIG: the ‘must have’ jig are the Williamson Benthos, river to sea Sea Rock, Hooker from Sevenseas, Hots Y2, and Maria Deep Sea Flower. Size from 180 to 300 gr.

TERMINAL TACKLE: There are many hooks on the market, but we recommend Fisherman, Hots, Gamakatsu, and Decoy.

Shore and flat fishing

In terms of wading, we strongly recommend:

  • Walking in the flat along with your medium-light rod and looking for Triggerfish, GT, and different kinds of Trevally, and Barracuda.

  • getting off the islands and walking on the reef’s edge, carrying your heavy equipment, and casting outside to tempt the chance with big GT, Napoleon, Barracuda, and Shark, all fish that are caught from shore can provide a considerable dose of excitement and adrenaline.

ROD: for sight fishing, the best equipment is composed of a ¾ ounce

REELS: the best option can be a medium-light reel like Stella 5000 or other reels of the same size with decent drag and gear.

LINE: 20-30 lb braid line and a 40-50 lb shock leader.

LURES: a good selection is composed of some minnow and lipless minnow, a small popper, a stick of 10-12 cm, some metal jig, and some jig headset with soft bait.

Especially for the Giant Parrotfish, a soft crab assembled with a heavy-duty hook and some lead can be the definitive solution.

Fishing from the reef’s edge is possible to use the same tackle from offshore fishing, the best lures in these conditions are sinking stickbait around 100 gr and pencil bait of the same size.

At the moment Sudan is the last new in the world of fly fishing destination.

item.title: Chi siamo
item.content:encoded:
PROFILO AZIENDALE

Wild Sea Expedition nasce dalla nostra grande passione per la pesca e per visitare  zone selvaggie e sconosciute, specializzati dal 2012 in pesca in mare al GT.

Siamo una piccola squadra di giovani esploratori che per primi hanno esplorato il potenziale di pesca sportiva nel Sud del Mar Rosso (Sudan, Eritrea e Gibuti), e nel Golfo di Aden e Oceano Indiano (Yemen, Somaliland ) alla scoperta di luoghi al di fuori dei percorsi turistici.

Abbiamo iniziato a viaggiare ed esplorare a 20 anni, e questo ci ha permesso di costruirci una grande esperienza sia di pesca, che di ricerca di pesci e zone, ma soprattutto nella gestione delle varie situazioni che si possono creare in aree così remote. Negli ultimi anni abbiamo fatto più di 10 diverse grandi spedizione esplorative in cinque paesi diversi.

Questa passione per la scoperta ci ha portato a gestire due barche da crociera in Sudan, e un campo mobile per viaggi itineranti nell’isola di Socotra.

MISSIONE

Il nostro scopo è continuare a scoprire mete incontaminate, al fine di offrire ai pescatori appassionati e fanatici la possibilità di pescare alcuni degli ultimi paradisi terrestri.

Pensiamo che ogni viaggio sia una grande opportunità per comprendere a fondo il pianeta che abitiamo, di conseguenza Wild Sea Expedition è lieta di offrire ai suoi clienti non solo l’esperienza di pesca, ma anche esperienze naturalistiche e culturali.


ETICA

Wild Sea Expedition si fonda su questi basi, al fine di avere un impatto minore possibile:

Operiamo in modo responsabile a sostegno della conservazione ambientale;

Ad eccezione dello stretto necessario per il nostro consumo, pratichiamo rigorosamente il catch and release, ed ogni pesce viene trattato con cura e rispetto;

Utilizziamo sempre e solo ami senza ardiglione, per un maggior rispetto dei pesci e per ragioni di sicurezza in barca;

Implementiamo costantemente i nostri mezzi, barche, attrezzature e itinerari, per offrire un sempre miglior servizio di anno in anno.

SEGUI IL NOSTRO VIAGGIO

View fullsize
View fullsize
View fullsize
View fullsize

SQUADRA

Nicola Vitali

è nato in Italia nel 1986 e pesca da quando aveva 4 anni. Inizia a viaggiare per la pesca all'età di 18 anni, visitando Australia, Nepal, Irlanda, Marocco, Maldive, Oman, Mauritius, Nicaragua, Perù, India, Egitto, Sudan, Arabia Saudita, Gibuti, Eritrea e Yemen, sempre attratto da nuove e sconosciute destinazioni. Dopo essersi laureato in ingegneria civile e ambientale inizia a cercare alcune delle ultime frontiere per la pesca, scoprendo gli enormi Gts dell'isola di Socotra dove organizza un campo di pesca e le barriere coralline vergini del Sudan. Lo troverai come trip manager in Sudan o a Socotra, e ti guiderà durante il tuo viaggio, a popping, jigging o pesca a mosca. Parla italiano, inglese e francese e sta imparando l'arabo. È capitano certificato per navigare con barche fino a 24 m senza limiti di distanza dalla costa. Durante il suo tempo libero in Sudan, testa nuovi spot, tecniche e attrezzature. Collabora anche con diverse riviste di pesca da tutto il mondo.

Federico Castignoli

 è nato in Italia nel 1987, pesca da quando aveva 4 anni e non si fermerà mai. A 18 anni inizia a viaggiare per la pesca e per il kayak, e grazie a queste due passioni, in alcuni anni ha visitato Maldive, Mauritius, India, Irlanda, Svezia, Cile, Argentina, Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Egitto, Eritrea, Sudan e Yemen. Lo troverai come responsabile del viaggio e guida nel Mar Rosso e come guida di pesca a Socotra, e si unisce anche a ogni viaggio esplorativo. Nonostante il suo aspetto rilassato, è una macchina da pesca e una guida molto seria ed esperta, alla fine del tuo viaggio con lui avrai bisogno di una vacanza. Parla italiano, inglese e spagnolo e durante il suo tempo libero in mare esplora nuovi luoghi e nuove attrezzature da pesca. Durante i mesi off dalla stagione di esca lavora come guida di rafting in Italia e nel mondo.

David Fernández Miguélez

è nato in Spagna nel 1995 e ha iniziato a pescare all'età di 4 anni. Essendo un ossessionato pescatore di lucci ha una forte passione per i pesci predatori e all'età di 18 anni ha iniziato a viaggiare in Spagna e in alcuni paesi europei come Danimarca, Irlanda, Belgio… Parla spagnolo e inglese. Dopo aver terminato gli studi come Tecnico Avanzato di Telecomunicazione Superiore ha deciso di lavorare nel mondo della pesca a mosca e ora fa parte del Wild Sea Expedition Team. Attualmente sta guidando in Sudan e con lui non perderai un colpo a tutti i pesci degli appartamenti. Lavora anche come fly tyer e cerca sempre di sviluppare nuovi modelli di mosca.

Robert Pljuscec

è nato in Croazia nel 1982, ha pescato il suo primo pesce da bambino e da allora è appassionato di pesca. Crescendo ha mostrato molto interesse per la natura e altre culture attraverso le riviste NG che suo padre gli stava portando nella fase iniziale della sua vita. Tutto ciò ha portato in seguito alla fotografia, alla videografia e alla guida, prima locale che internazionale con Wild Sea Expedition.

I NOSTRI PARTNER

item.title: Spedizioni
item.content:encoded:
SPEDIZIONI

PESCA SOCOTRA: MONSTER GT

L'isola, lunga circa 120 km, è considerata una delle isole più ventose del mondo, e viene battuta da correnti oceaniche molto forti, fattori che rendono il mare impraticabile per circa 7 mesi l'anno nei luoghi più produttivi. L'isola è conosciuta anche per i suoi numerosi alberi endemici chiamati sangue di drago e numerose altre specie di piante, uccelli, rettili e insetti che vivono solo qui, tanto da essere appellata la Galapagos dell'Oceano Indiano, ed essere riconosciuta come un patrimonio naturale dell’umanità dall'UNESCO.

L'isola è poco popolata, non ci sono strutture ricettive con l'eccezione di poche campeggio spartano, i villaggi di pescatori sono pochi e lontani da tutto, a volte raggiungibili solo in barca.

Gli spot di pesca inoltre sono spesso spettacolari, con alte scogliere a picco sul mare, dune di sabbia, isole selvagge e disabitate, tutti elementi che contribuiscono a farci sentire in un’epoca preistorica.

PESCA IN SUDAN: NUBIAN REEF

Il viaggio parte da Port Sudan, a bordo delle nostre barche MSY Elegante e MY Don Questo.

Il Mar Rosso Sudanese rappresenta oggi una destinazione quasi del tutto impescata, grazie al fatto di avere circa 650 km di costa, praticamente privi di insediamenti umani, ad eccezione di qualche villagio di pescatori.

PESCA IN SUDAN: NUBIAN FLAT

Al momento il Sudan è l'ultima novità nel mondo delle destinazione di pesca a mosca, e questo rende il viaggio ancora più eccitante dato il quantitativo di flats e zone ancora da esplorare., Durante la prima stagione esplorativa abbiamo scoperto stupendi flats vergini, realmente infestati di Triggerfish, pesce ancora poco conosciuto ma veramente eccitante da pescare, spesso in acqua molto bassa

Inoltre sono presenti in buona quantità GT, Red Snapper e Bluefin Trevally, ma anche Permit, Milkfish, Bumphead Parrotfish ed enormi Bonefish, e altre specie da barriera corallina sono presenti e possibili da catturare.
